data.title: Trump Escalates Fight With Media, Bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico From White House, Warns More Could Face Same Fate
data.description:
President Donald Trump banned CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House on Friday, citing what he called “FAKE NEWS” coverage of his administration.

In his Truth Social post, Trump wrote that outlets “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES” about his administration. He warned other news organizations could face similar restrictions.

Later, taking questions from reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said there was no single story behind the decision. “It’s really just cumulative stories over the last few years, you get sick of it,” he said, adding that outlets “purposely write negative news” to “diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration.”

When asked what the ban would involve, the U.S. President said, “I don’t want them in my office. I don’t want them here. I would say the ban would go as far as you can.”

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth backed the move on X, saying the Department of War “fully supports” the decision to have the outlets publish “from outside the White House.” He said the outlets had already “self-deport[ed] from the Pentagon,” accusing them of endangering troops with “false stories, leaks, and” fictional accounts of the president and U.S. forces.

Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right.”

Politico, owned by privately held Axel Springer, wrote on X that it “will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones” and would “vigorously defend” its First Amendment rights “against any attempt to restrict them.” The outlet added that claims it received government subsidies “are false and have been thoroughly debunked.”

data.title: Trump Escalates Economic Pressure on Russia With New Sanctions Law That Could Hit Moscow’s Biggest Trading Partners With Tariffs
data.description:
President Donald Trump has signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law that expands U.S. economic pressure on Moscow.

Trump Signs Russia Sanctions Bill Into Law

On Friday, Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law, according to the White House. The House passed the bill Wednesday after the Senate approved it last month.

It "authorizes and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran," the statement read.

The legislation expands sanctions targeting Russia’s energy and defense sectors and its so-called "shadow fleet" of tankers used to circumvent existing restrictions, Reuters reported.

The measure is intended to restrict revenue that supports Russia’s war in Ukraine by targeting key parts of its economy and energy trade.

New Tariff Powers Target Russia Trading Partners

The law also authorizes tariffs against major buyers of Russian energy, potentially extending the economic pressure beyond Moscow. The publication noted that critics say that the legislation gives Trump broad authority to impose tariffs that could remain in effect beyond his presidency. The critics also raised concerns that the expanded tariff powers could create economic risks for countries that maintain significant trade ties with Russia.

Putin Says Russia Has Faced 30,000+ Sanctions

Earlier this month, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi that Russia has faced more than 30,000 sanctions, calling economic restrictions and trade barriers tools of geopolitical competition.

He said Russia has responded by strengthening ties with "reliable, predictable partners," while stating that its economy has grown faster than the global average over the past three years.

data.title: BlackRock clients buy $108M worth of Bitcoin through IBIT as institutional demand holds firm
data.description:
BlackRock clients purchased $108.44 million worth of Bitcoin in a single session through the firm's iShares Bitcoin Trust, known as IBIT. The figure lands squarely in the middle of what has become a remarkably consistent pattern for the fund, which has been logging daily inflows ranging from $80 million to over $200 million.

Since its launch in January 2024, IBIT has grown into the dominant force in US spot Bitcoin ETF market, routinely capturing between 50% and 80% of total daily or weekly inflows across all competing products. Grayscale's GBTC, once the only game in town for institutional Bitcoin exposure, has been on the other side of that trade, experiencing persistent outflows as investors rotate toward lower-fee alternatives.

IBIT's holdings have swelled to somewhere between 770,000 and 786,000 BTC, making BlackRock one of the largest institutional holders of Bitcoin on the planet, even though the firm itself holds none of it on its balance sheet. BlackRock only transacts in Bitcoin at the explicit request of clients, a structural detail that matters: the firm is a conduit, not a speculator.

Custody runs through Coinbase Prime, which handles the underlying Bitcoin on behalf of the trust.

Multi-day buying streaks have pushed cumulative weekly inflows past $680 million during certain weeks. The scale of ongoing demand suggests this is not a novelty trade. Institutions are allocating to Bitcoin through IBIT the same way they allocate to gold through GLD: methodically, repeatedly, and in size.

BlackRock made a quiet but consequential product change in 2026, cutting the minimum threshold for in-kind conversions from $25 million down to $1 million. In plain terms, this means investors who already hold Bitcoin directly can swap their coins for IBIT shares at a much lower entry point than before.

Cumulative in-kind conversions surpassed $5 billion, as investors who were sitting on direct Bitcoin positions migrated into the regulated ETF wrapper. The motivations vary: cleaner tax reporting, easier custody, eligibility for certain institutional mandates that require regulated vehicles.

Dropping the minimum from $25 million to $1 million expanded participation to family offices, smaller RIAs, and high-net-worth individuals who were previously priced out of the conversion mechanism.

data.title: Warren Buffett's legacy: Investing lessons that defined the ‘Oracle of Omaha’
data.description:
Even in the age of algorithms, short attention spans and TikTok teases, Warren Buffett continued to profit with his patient bargain-hunting approach while offering folksy advice on investing and life.

As chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, Buffett became famous for his unwavering and methodical investing style: Buy good businesses when their prices are low, stay on the sidelines when prices are too high and be patient with well-chosen picks.

He rode that to decades of beating the rest of the US stock market before he retired as Berkshire’s chairman on Friday, September 18, less than a year after giving up his role as CEO.

The formula of buying good things at low prices sounds simple, and it’s the foundation of a style of investing called “value” hunting. But it periodically comes under criticism when the hot new thing is enthralling Wall Street, whether it’s dot-com stocks in the late 1990s or gold when its price was setting records early this year. (Buffett is famously sceptical of gold as an investment, saying it “has two significant shortcomings, being neither of much use nor procreative.”)

The investing world has had other celebrities. J.P. Morgan built his reputation by investing in railroads during the 19th century. Andrew Carnegie helped build the US steel industry and became famous for his philanthropy. Jim Cramer and Kevin O’Leary are on TV shows. But few ever cracked into the national consciousness like Buffett, and none did so from near the geographic centre of the country in Omaha, Nebraska.

Many professional investors also adhere to Buffett’s style of bargain-hunting. But none have had the kind of folksy humour and candour that can draw hordes of investors each year, like those attending Berkshire Hathaway’s annual shareholder meeting.

More than 40,000 people would pack an Omaha arena on the first Saturday in May to hear from Buffett and his longtime investing partner, Charlie Munger, who died in 2023 and espoused a similar take-it-slow and make-it-right approach to investing.

Besides talking about how they hunted for well-run businesses and the news of the day, they would also regularly confess to their own mistakes and crack wise.

“Not a day goes by where what I’ve learned about Warren doesn’t affect me positively, both personally and financially,” said Todd Finkle, a retired professor. He grew up in Omaha, knows Buffett’s children and wrote the book, “Warren Buffett: Investor and Entrepreneur.”

When Finkle would bring students to visit the “Oracle of Omaha” for extended Q-and-A meetings, Finkle said the first topic Buffett would discuss was never financial.

“He didn’t say anything about money. The first topic that he would always bring up is that the most important thing you’ll do in your life is to pick who to marry.”

Following a scandal at Salomon Brothers, in which Berkshire Hathaway had an ownership stake, Buffett became chairman and testified in Congress. He said all employees were told, “After they first obey all rules, I then want employees to ask themselves whether they are willing to have any contemplated act appear the next day on the front page of their local paper to be read by their spouses, children and friends with the reporting done by an informed and critical reporter.”

That reputation for honesty, along with his famed patience for investments, helped Buffett stay famous even in this “post-truth” era where people scroll through feeds at finger-flicking speed. He’s such an icon that scammers would use him in AI-generated videos that appeared to show him endorsing questionable investments or political candidates.

On Reddit’s WallStreetBets forum, traders share picks for potential get-rich-quick opportunities in day-trading stocks and options. The discussion jumps from idea to idea, but even the denizens there know Buffett and his famous advice to “be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful.”

His reputation is so strong and his advice so well-known that some memes on the forum ironically joke about doing the opposite, with a picture of Buffett suggesting that everyone freak out and sell in a panic.

Bob Miles, who has taught a college course about Buffett for 16 years, said that people might initially get attracted to Buffett because he is rich and has made many Berkshire shareholders wealthy. But their interest deepens after reading Buffett’s annual letters, which became required reading for many investors, and hearing him speak in interviews.

Through reading and listening, people would glean nuggets from Buffett like his core rules for investing: “Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget Rule No. 1.” Or that “you only find out who is swimming naked when the tide goes out,” referencing how tough times will quickly show who has been taking too much risk.

He also suggested that “who you associate with is just enormously important. Don’t expect that you’ll make every decision right on that. But you are going to have your life progress in the general direction of the people you work with, that you admire, that become your friends.”

“People associate him with successful investing, but I look at him more and more as kind of a guide toward how to live a successful life, whatever your talents happen to be,” Miles said.

At the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business, trips for students to Berkshire’s annual meetings were always a hot ticket. “I don’t know of any time that it wasn’t popular,” said David Musto, a finance professor at the school and faculty director of the Jacobs Master of Science in Quantitative Finance.

With Buffett’s departure from the stage, the obvious question is whether anyone else could replace him as the world’s most famous value investor.

Musto said some other big names still exist in the investing world, such as Will Danoff at Fidelity Investments, who is retiring from day-to-day management at the end of the year. But it’s difficult to find someone with as strong and as long a track record as Buffett’s. Or the wit and personality.

Musto said it’s important for value investing to remain a force in the market, particularly when traders are jumping into meme stocks, obscure cryptocurrencies and other bets built more on hope that their prices will go up than belief that it’s a good business trading at a good price.

“It certainly helps to have people in the middle,” Musto said, “thinking about the value of a stock.”

data.description:
By Tanner Brown

China spent decades trying to limit the number of babies its citizens had. Now Beijing is sending new parents cash.

More than 25 million infants and toddlers have received China's 2026 child-care subsidy, a tax-free payment of 3,600 yuan, or about $530, a year for every child under three. Another roughly 24 million children have benefited from a policy eliminating child-care and education fees for the final year of kindergarten.

The demographic question is whether that is enough to persuade Chinese couples to have another child. Probably not by itself. The more immediate question for investors is what happens when Beijing puts tens of billions of yuan directly into the hands of young families at a time when Chinese consumers remain unusually reluctant to spend.

Retail sales rose just 1.2% in the first seven months of 2026 from a year earlier, while goods sales increased 1.1%. Against that backdrop, 3,600 yuan isn't trivial: It is equivalent to about 12% of China's per capita consumer spending last year.

The program also represents a change in how Beijing is trying to support demand. China's recent consumer stimulus has leaned heavily on subsidies for purchases such as cars and appliances. The child-care money is different. It arrives as cash and isn't tied to a particular product.

That makes diapers, formula, baby food, children's clothing, and healthcare obvious potential beneficiaries. For consumer companies, the best-positioned businesses may be those already finding ways to grow despite China's shrinking population of babies.

Procter & Gamble is one. The Pampers maker said organic baby-care sales in Greater China jumped 20% in its fiscal year ended June, even as the category grew only in the low single digits globally. P&G says its China business is expanding in premium and superpremium diapers, reflecting a potentially important shift: Chinese parents may be having fewer children, but many are willing to spend more on each one.

Formula makers are seeing a similar opportunity. Danone said its Asia-Pacific sales rose 5.2% in the second quarter, citing competitive growth in infant formula in China. Chinese dairy giant Mengniu did even better: Its milk-formula business grew more than 30% on a comparable basis in the first half of 2026. China Feihe, one of the country's biggest infant-formula specialists, reported a 2.3% rise in first-half revenue after sales fell sharply last year, with the company attributing the rebound partly to growth in some infant-formula lines.

China may have fewer babies, but spending on each baby is proving surprisingly resilient.

The effect probably shouldn't be overstated. Shi Wei, a researcher at Beijing Institute of Technology, expects the subsidy's overall impact on consumption to be relatively modest and concentrated in child-related spending. "The more important significance of the child-care subsidy lies in its role as a social-policy safety net and its signaling effect, rather than as a powerful economic stimulus tool," she said.

The biggest constraint is simple: There are still fewer babies. China recorded just 7.92 million births in 2025. A few thousand yuan a year does little to offset the much larger costs of housing, education, child-care, and lost income associated with raising a child.

That means investors should be careful about treating the subsidy as a demographic turnaround story. Its more plausible near-term effect is to raise spending per child rather than the number of children.

That distinction is also being made inside China. "The subsidy's effect on raising births will be relatively gradual in the short term, while its effect on boosting consumption will be more direct," said She Yu, a senior researcher at the State Council's Development Research Center.

He argues that cash transferred directly to families should increase demand for everything from formula and diapers to toys, clothing and child-care services.

That could favor premium diapers, formula, and health products more than mass-market baby goods. It could also help China's e-commerce platforms. Online sales of physical goods rose 4.6% in the first seven months of this year, far faster than overall goods consumption.

The policy matters beyond baby products, too. When Beijing launched the national subsidy, the central government set aside about 90 billion yuan to support it. It was China's first nationwide cash subsidy specifically for families with children under three. Free preschool adds another layer of savings.

That is still small relative to China's economy. But it is a notable experiment in a country where policymakers have historically been much more comfortable subsidizing factories and infrastructure than sending money directly to households.

For P&G, Danone, Mengniu, Feihe, and the online platforms selling their products, the question is no longer whether the money is coming. It is how much of it families decide to spend.

data.title: EU to impose provisional safeguards to protect electrical steel from imports
data.description:
The European
Union will impose a set of import ‌quotas and minimum prices for
electrical steel and downstream ​products, it said on Friday, in
a bid to ⁠shield the EU from cheap imports, principally from
Asia.

The move will benefit Thyssenkrupp's steel unit
TKMS and Poland's Stalprodukt SA, among the last
European ‌producers of electrical steel, which is used in wind
turbines and power grids.

To keep production in Europe ‌going, the EU will establish
'safeguards' in the form ‌of ⁠quotas for grain-oriented electrical
steel (GOES), as well as laminations ⁠and transformer cores
containing the metal. For the steel itself, the minimum price
will be set between €2,800 and €3,400 per metric ton within the
quotas and at €3,500 ​per ton for volumes ‌above them.

The European Commission launched an investigation into
safeguards for GOES in March. The measures to apply from
September 25 are provisional, while the investigation continues.
Definitive measures, at the ‌end of the investigation, would
require a qualified majority ​of EU members to be imposed.

Electrical steel was not covered by broader measures imposed
earlier this year ⁠to protect Europe's struggling steel sector,
which has come under intense pressure from low-cost competition,
including from China.

Thyssenkrupp last year announced ‌temporary production stops
at its electrical steel sites in Germany and France as a result
of rivals selling excess capacity on the European markets at
what sources have said are 25% discounts.

Brussels' move comes as the continent's industry is
increasingly calling for better protection against China,
the EU's second-largest trading partner ‌after the United States,
with automotive, chemicals and steel firms all facing ​pressure.

Imports of electrical steel from China, Japan, Russia, South
Korea and the United States have been subject ⁠to anti-dumping
measures, also in the form of minimum import prices, ⁠since 2015.
The new minimum prices, while not strictly comparable, are
significantly higher than those already in place. They ‌will also
apply to downstream products.

China represented more than 50 per cent of EU imports of the steel
and its downstream ​products in 2025.

data.title: Morgan Stanley's MSBT ETF buys $52M in Bitcoin, sees no outflows
data.description:
Morgan Stanley's spot Bitcoin ETF has been on a shopping spree. The Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust, ticker MSBT, scooped up roughly 642 BTC worth approximately $50.6 million through a series of transfers from Coinbase Prime over a two-week stretch in September 2026. And in a detail that would make any fund manager jealous, the product has recorded essentially no net outflows since its April launch.

The MSBT has pulled in cumulative net inflows exceeding $538 million, pushing its total net assets to somewhere between $586 million and $635 million by mid-September. For a product that represents Wall Street's old guard tiptoeing into Bitcoin territory, those numbers are more than a toe.

Morgan Stanley launched MSBT on April 8, 2026, making it the first spot Bitcoin ETF from a major US bank-affiliated asset manager.

The fund's first month set the tone. MSBT pulled in $193.6 million in net inflows across its initial 30 days, with only a single recorded day of net outflows in its entire history.

The product charges a 0.14% expense ratio, which made it the cheapest spot Bitcoin ETF at launch. Coinbase Custody handles the actual Bitcoin storage, while BNY Mellon serves as administrator. The fund tracks the CoinDesk Bitcoin Benchmark Rate.

The September accumulation, visible through on-chain data, showed multiple transfers flowing from Coinbase Prime into the fund's wallets. Roughly $50.6 million in Bitcoin moved across those transactions over about two weeks, suggesting steady creation of new ETF shares to meet ongoing demand rather than a single large institutional buy.

The majority of inflows have been driven by self-directed clients, not Morgan Stanley's financial advisors. That distinction matters. Morgan Stanley manages trillions in client assets through its wealth management division, and if the advisor channel hasn't fully engaged yet, the current numbers represent something closer to the floor than the ceiling.

Self-directed clients are essentially people who log into their Morgan Stanley accounts and buy the ETF on their own, without a financial advisor recommending it. These are investors who already know they want Bitcoin exposure and are choosing to get it through a familiar, regulated wrapper rather than buying crypto directly.

data.title: Disney Escalates Fight With Trump Administration, Asks Judge to Block FCC’s Unusual Early Review of 8 ABC Licenses
data.description:
Walt Disney Co. (NYSE:DIS) is asking a U.S. judge to halt an early Federal Communications Commission review of eight ABC station licenses, arguing the process is being used to pressure the network over coverage critical of President Donald Trump.

Disney Challenges FCC Review

Disney and ABC said in a court filing that FCC Chair Brendan Carr has been carrying out directives from Trump that target speech critical of the administration, Reuters reported.

The companies argue the FCC’s unusually early review amounts to retaliation for disfavored news and entertainment programming.

Disney, ABC and the FCC did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

The FCC ordered the reviews in April, even though the stations’ licenses were not scheduled for renewal until October 2028. The agency had not ordered such an early review in more than 50 years.

The move came shortly after Trump called for ABC to fire late-night host Jimmy Kimmel.

Read Also: Bob Iger Leaves Disney (Again): Here's What Happened The Last Time He Stepped Down

Trump, FCC Face Free Speech Fight

Disney also cited Trump’s criticism of journalists, including NBC’s Kristen Welker and an ABC White House reporter. Trump has also called for broadcasters to face consequences over programming and coverage he opposes.

ABC has more than 200 affiliated stations across the U.S., but Disney directly owns eight of them, all of which are now under the FCC’s scrutiny.

Last year, Trump criticized negative media coverage, arguing that when 97% of stories about someone are unfavorable, it is "no longer free speech" but "cheating."

Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) had called the Trump administration’s actions "blatant attacks" on the free press. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) similarly criticized threats against ABC’s licenses.

data.title: Hong Kong sets out initiatives to secure long-term development of pillar industries
data.description:
EQS Newswire / 19/09/2026 / 07:30 CET/CEST

HONG KONG SAR - Media OutReach Newswire - 19 September 2026 - Hong Kong's Chief Executive John Lee rolled out various measures to develop Hong Kong's key economic centres when he unveiled the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) (2026-2030) and his fifth Policy Address on September 16.

Under Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will focus on strengthening the four centres, developing the hub for high-calibre talent, consolidating and enhancing its competitive edge as an international city.

Factsheets: Hong Kong's New Chapter / The Story Begins Hong Kong's status as world-renowned international financial, maritime and trade centres as well as an international aviation hub underpin the city's high-quality development and provide a firm foundation for the city's long-term stability and prosperity. "We will consolidate and enhance Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, and stay committed to our global positioning," Mr Lee said. "Hong Kong will deepen the development of its global offshore Renminbi business and capital market, develop an international asset and wealth management centre and international risk management centre, enhance the securities market and expand fixed income and commodity trading." Hong Kong has become the world's largest cross‑boundary wealth management centre this year, and the HKSAR Government will continue to develop a more attractive asset and wealth management ecosystem, Mr Lee said. Hong Kong will develop a commodity trading ecosystem with gold as an entry point by driving the development of the clearing system, storage, supply, and infrastructure related to gold trading. The city's central clearing and settlement system for gold will be officially launched in the first quarter of 2027. "The significance of the First Five-Year Plan for Hong Kong lies in a mindset shift; we must plan Hong Kong's financial development with a longer-term vision and broader perspective to adapt with flexibility and diversity," said Christopher Hui, Hong Kong's Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury. "Each of our initiatives centres around one objective, which is to elevate Hong Kong from a 'corridor of capital' to a 'destination of choice'." Hong Kong was ranked the world's fifth‑largest entity in merchandise trade in 2025. The HKSAR Government announced plans to consolidate and enhance Hong Kong's status as an international trade centre, playing a greater role in the high‑level opening up of the Chinese Mainland. Since the Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global was established last October, it has provided assistance, including listing and raising capital in Hong Kong, aligning with overseas standards, acquiring industry certifications and fulfilling compliance requirements for more than 340 Mainland enterprises. The Task Force will strengthen collaboration with professional organisations to train talent for the GoGlobal initiative and enhance professional services, among other areas. "In alignment with the National 15th Five-Year Plan's call to advocate and practise true multilateralism, the First Five-Year Plan proposes to continue expanding international economic and trade network," said Algernon Yau, Hong Kong's Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development. "We will actively forge free trade agreements and investment agreements with economies that are of development potential or strategic locations. Meanwhile, we will expand our network of overseas offices, and leverage the combined networks of our overseas Economic and Trade Offices, InvestHK, and the Hong Kong Trade Development Council offices globally to deepen overseas ties and step up trade and investment promotion." As an international maritime centre, Hong Kong has ranked fourth globally in maritime comprehensive strength for seven consecutive years. The Five-Year Plan will drive a "volume to value" transformation of the Hong Kong Port, capitalising on its strengths in high value‑added maritime services, to develop Hong Kong into a "Global Maritime Capital". To promote high value-added services, the industry will develop "Finance + Shipping". Taking advantage of the city's well‑established maritime finance, insurance and maritime arbitration under common law, Hong Kong will build an integrated ecosystem under which Hong Kong‑invested enterprises adopt Hong Kong law, take out Hong Kong insurance and choose for arbitration to be seated in Hong Kong. Regarding aviation, Hong Kong's passenger throughput recorded a year‑on‑year increase of 15% last year, to 61 million, with flights to over 220 destinations. The city's air cargo throughput reached 5.07 million tonnes, making its airport the world's busiest cargo airport for the 15th year since 2010. To strengthen development as international aviation hub, Hong Kong will expand its aviation network, and diversify business opportunities. The HKSAR Government will continue to take the initiative to visit South America, Africa, Central Asia, the Middle East and the Caucasus to expedite the conclusion of new air services agreements and the expansion of traffic rights, thereby assisting the industry in exploring new passenger and cargo sources. As for building Hong Kong as an international innovation and technology centre, the HKSAR Government will step up its efforts to promote artificial intelligence (AI) applications across various trades, and continue to strike a balance between encouraging innovation and protecting security, thereby enhancing Hong Kong's international competitiveness in AI development. In alignment with the national strategic technology areas, Hong Kong will focus on core technologies such as life and health, AI and robotics, microelectronics, new energy, advanced manufacturing and new materials. It will also continue to raise the ratio of Total Domestic Expenditure on Innovation Activities to Gross Domestic Product, striving to reach 3% after 2030. data.title: Markets Espresso: Can Tatas say Tata to Drama; What all can you do in ₹4.5 lakh?
data.description:
Hello there, Espresso lovers! You know, out of the 365 days in a year, you'll find Mumbaikars complain about crowded trains, potholes, traffic and whatnot for 355 of them, yet go about their business diligently. But these 10 other days are Bappa time! When Bappa is here, the city feels different, the vibe feels different, the fervour feels different, and during these 10 days, the complaints, cribbing, everything takes a backseat. We can only pray to the Vighnaharta to get rid of all the Vighnas in our lives, and in the markets as well! For the markets, there are plenty of them!

If you wanted to use rose petals to find the answer to "will he or won't he", you would've emptied out the entire garden before getting the answer. The "he" in question? Kevin Warsh. The new Fed Chair. More secretive than secret itself. He eventually did. Pulled the trigger. Raised rates by 25 basis points, the first time in three years. He had to. He was caught in a "idhar kua, udhar khai" situation (Devil and the Deep Blue Sea). If he did not raise rates now, the fact that he was controlled by the White House would be firmly established. If he did, brickbats were certain from the White House.

Of course, Donald Trump was not pleased with the decision but still has words of praise for Mr Warsh. He blamed the "hostile" Fed board behind the rate decision, and still wants the US to have the lowest interest rates anywhere in the world. Well, we started the year projecting that the Fed would CUT thrice this year, but then someone decided to have an adventure in Iran that has now gone on for seven months, and those three rate cuts have turned into three rate HIKES. Yikes! Nobody lets the greatest President of all time live in peace. Boo Hoo! The dot plot even suggests that there might be more to come! Wonder how long he will continue to have the same words of praise for Mr Warsh. Your guess is as good as ours.

There's an old saying - Charity begins at home. The Tatas have taken that seriously, and we are extremely proud of that. However, if they wanted to produce a daily soap, they could've done one in Film City, not at Bombay House. Charity begins at home; daily soaps don't. The second season of Kahaani Tata Sons Ke Board Room Ki is currently being shot at the Bombay House. The cast includes Noel Tata, N Chandrasekaran, Venu Srinivasan, other members of the board, and an extended cameo by the SP Group. Who plays what character? We'll let you decide that. Casting isn't our forte.

The RBI wants Tata Sons to list. Noel Tata Doesn't. The Board wants N Chandrasekaran to stay as Chairman for another five years. Maybe he does, maybe he doesn't, but Noel Tata doesn't want that either. The board overruled him in a vote. He called the vote illegal. He now wants to take the matter to the AGM, where he plans on voting Chandra out. The SP Group is all in for Tata Sons to list, calling it a "social and moral imperative." That social and moral imperative will also enable them to monetise their own stake and bring their own spiralling debt situation under control (that's in brackets/asterisk). This needs to end soon. The credibility and pride of India's most trusted and loved business houses are at stake. They have their task cut out, so do we. Guess our friend Rachna Dhanrajani has many more newsbreaks lined up from Bombay House. She couldn't be happier!

While this drama continues, another might just be coming to an end soon enough. HDFC Bank, as our friend Ritu Singh reports, could well be on course to announce its successor to Sashidhar Jagdishan soon, maybe as early as this weekend. Whoever it may be - Kaizad Bharucha or Anup Bagchi- it will be a difficult choice for them to make as to what should be their first priority: clean up the bank's battered image, or continue to focus on the business, hoping that if that does well, the image will clean itself up. We are waiting to see this chapter flash "THE END" and find out who gets on the hot seat of India's largest private lender.

If you all were wondering why the iPhone did not get a mention in the previous episode, it took me that long to process the fact that a mobile phone could also cost ₹4 lakh. Oh wait, ₹4,49,900 to be precise. So if someone gives ₹4.5 lakh in cash or writes a cheque, will they return the 100 bucks as change? Maybe. Will be helpful for the auto fare to get back home. What all can you do with ₹4.5 lakh? Have a luxury holiday? Pay rent for 6-7 months in Mumbai (In other cities it could be a year or even more)? Shell out 90% of the payment for a car? But that's for non-iPhone Paglus. For the iPhone Paglus, they were queued up outside the Apple stores in Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru from the early hours of the morning to lay their hands on the new iPhone 18 and PRO MAX. The Duo, yes, that same kidney-burning priced phone, begins to sell on October 23. Don't be surprised to see a long queue for that either. Tell us in the comments what all you would do if you had ₹4.5 lakh.

Where are oil prices headed? JPMorgan says we don't know. Yes. That was one confession that stirred the market chatter all through Friday. Their note says it is increasingly difficult to establish a baseline scenario for oil because they just don't know what the endgame for the Iran war is. They have also warned that if there is no diplomatic breakthrough between Trump and Xi next week, it will be very difficult to believe in the assumption that this oil supply disruption is temporary.

By the time it's next Saturday, Bappa would have headed home, leaving us all emo yet again; NSE, whose IPO has been fully subscribed, would have become a listed company, and BSE would be days away from being called a Nifty 50 constituent, while Wipro, for the first time, will no longer be part of the benchmark index. But what happens in Iran? What will Donald Trump do? Will there be a solution to this sooner? The answer to that is what JPMorgan said: We don't know. Next week will also be the 15th Episode of Markets Espresso. For all the love, reads, comments and subscriptions, we are very grateful! Do like, share, subscribe and follow us on our social media handles as well. Until then, Ganpati Bappa Morya!

data.title: Maldives Clears $150 Mn Debt To India After $50 Mn Tranche Payment
data.description:
MEA said the treasury bills subscribed by SBI in 2019 were extended six times, while India covered nearly USD 45 million in interest

The Maldives has repaid a USD 150 million loan to India after settling the final USD 50 million tranche of treasury bills subscribed by the State Bank of India (SBI) in 2019. The final payment was completed on September 17.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed the repayment during his regular media briefing on Friday. He said the final tranche of USD 50 million, part of the total USD 150 million subscribed by SBI with the Maldivian government, had been successfully settled.

SBI had originally subscribed to the treasury bills in 2019, after which the arrangement was extended six times. Each extension was for one year, with the Maldivian government eventually settling the principal amount of the treasury bills.

While the Maldives paid the principal, the Indian government covered the interest payments on the USD 150 million treasury bills during the past five years. Jaiswal said the total interest settlement made by India was close to USD 45 million.

India Provides Financial Support

India has also extended a Rs 30 billion currency swap facility to the Maldives as part of its financial support for the neighbouring country. Jaiswal said the facility was intended to support the Maldivian financial system and strengthen bilateral financial cooperation.

In addition to the currency swap arrangement, the Indian government has subscribed to USD 350 million worth of treasury bonds issued by the Maldives. These bonds are valid until 2029 and 2030, providing another component of India’s ongoing financial engagement with the country.

India’s engagement with the Maldives extends beyond financial assistance, with essential commodity supplies forming part of the broader development cooperation between the two countries. The partnership covers financial, economic and development-related areas.

Jaiswal described the relationship as a longstanding development partnership between India and the Maldives. “India and Maldives have a longstanding development partnership,” he said, highlighting the broader cooperation alongside the recent completion of the treasury bill repayment.

data.title: Cash-Flow Lending Key To Financing New-Age Industries: SBI
data.description:
State Bank of India is exploring lending models based on future cash flows as new-age businesses often lack the traditional collateral required for bank finance

Cash-flow-based lending is set to become increasingly important for financing new-age industries such as data centres, solar manufacturing and technology-driven businesses, State Bank of India Managing Director Ashwini Kumar Tewari said on Friday.

Speaking at a financial market conclave hosted by the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Tewari said banks need to develop new lending models as emerging businesses may not have the tangible security traditionally required for bank finance.

“Unless banks are able to find ways to fund these kinds of new businesses,” banks will need to move beyond relying only on collateral, Tewari said, pointing to sectors such as pharmaceuticals and technology.

SBI Explores Cash-Flow-Based Lending

Tewari said State Bank of India (SBI) is already evaluating cash-flow-based lending and applying the approach to emerging sectors. The bank calls its model CHAKRA, which it is using to assess businesses where conventional security may not be adequate.

The approach requires lenders to assess a business based on its expected revenue and ability to generate cash rather than relying primarily on physical assets as collateral.

Tewari said this could become particularly relevant for businesses such as data centres, solar manufacturing and other technology-led industries, where the underlying assets and business models can differ significantly from traditional industries.

Technology Assessment Key To Lending Decisions

However, financing such businesses also presents challenges for banks. Tewari said lenders need to understand the technology involved, its revenue potential and the economics of the project before deciding on financing.

He cited the solar sector as an example, saying SBI had examined the technology used in projects and found that some technologies were already outdated. Different technologies can also have different power-generation economics, making it difficult for banks to assess the likely revenue and cash-flow generation of a project.

The ability to establish future revenue and cash flows therefore remains a key challenge for lenders looking to expand financing to new-age sectors, Tewari said.

The shift towards cash-flow-based lending could allow banks to finance businesses that have limited traditional collateral but have identifiable revenue streams and viable operating models.

data.title: Dr Reddy’s, Takeda Partner To Distribute First Approved Dengue Vaccine In India
data.description:
The exclusive private-market partnership will make Takeda’s QDENGA available for pediatric and adult vaccination, with launch expected in H1 2027

Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories and Takeda Pharmaceutical Company have entered into an exclusive distribution agreement to promote and distribute Takeda’s QDENGA dengue vaccine across India’s private market for pediatric and adult vaccination, with availability expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory processes. The vaccine received marketing authorisation from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) in July 2026 for people aged 4-60 years, making it the first dengue vaccine approved in India.

Under the agreement, Dr. Reddy’s will handle promotion and distribution in the private market, while Takeda will retain rights for the public market along with overall medical and brand oversight. The companies will also undertake healthcare-professional engagement and disease-awareness activities related to dengue vaccination.

Addressing Dengue Burden

The partnership comes as dengue continues to pose a public-health challenge in India. The companies said reported dengue cases have increased 11-fold over the past two decades, while nationwide surveillance has identified circulation of all four dengue virus serotypes across multiple regions. A study cited by the companies found that one in 14 patients had concurrent infection with multiple serotypes.

“As the second-largest vaccine player in India, we believe the introduction of India’s first approved dengue vaccine is an important development for the country’s healthcare landscape,” said M.V. Ramana, CEO - Global Generics, Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories. “Through our collaboration with Takeda, we look forward to making QDENGA available to eligible individuals and contributing to efforts aimed at addressing the country’s dengue burden,” he added.

Dr. Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets, International Business Unit, Takeda, said the partnership would support private-market access while the company continues to work towards broader dengue-prevention efforts. The vaccine has been approved in 43 countries since 2022, according to Takeda, with more than 32 million doses distributed worldwide. QDENGA is also included in the World Health Organization’s List of Prequalified Vaccines. The collaboration combines Takeda’s experience in dengue vaccine development and disease education with Dr. Reddy’s commercial and healthcare network in India.

Takeda said its longer-term dengue strategy includes supporting surveillance, awareness, vector control and community engagement. The company has also welcomed a recent Parliamentary Committee recommendation to consider dengue vaccination under India’s Universal Immunization Programme.

data.title: UPI MDR Above Rs 2,000 Seen Having Limited Ebitda Impact On Consumer Firms: Report
data.description:
Nykaa and DMart could see the highest profitability impact, while QSRs and food delivery platforms are largely insulated due to lower average transaction values, says Elara Securities

Potentially introducing a 0.4 per cent merchant discount rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions above Rs 2,000 is unlikely to materially affect the profitability of most consumer discretionary and internet companies, according to a report by Elara Securities. The brokerage estimates that average order values remain below the proposed threshold for most businesses, limiting the impact on FY27 earnings. Nykaa and DMart are expected to face the highest exposure, at 2.6 per cent and 2.1 per cent of FY27 estimated Ebitda, respectively.

Nykaa And DMart Face Higher Exposure

Elara estimates that Nykaa would see the highest consolidated Ebitda impact among the companies analysed, with an incremental MDR cost of around Rs 299 million, equivalent to 2.6 per cent of FY27 estimated Ebitda. Its beauty and personal care business has an estimated average net sales value of Rs 1,567, while Nykaa Fashion has an average order value of around Rs 1,759, putting a relatively larger proportion of transactions above the Rs 2,000 threshold.

DMart is estimated to face an incremental cost of around Rs 1.27 billion, translating into a 2.1 per cent impact on FY27 Ebitda. Elara attributes the relatively higher exposure to DMart's estimated average order value of Rs 1,668 and its large transaction base. Around 40 per cent of its transactions are estimated to become MDR-liable after factoring in the UPI mix.

The report notes that recovering the additional cost could be more challenging for DMart because of its value positioning and price-sensitive customer base. Nykaa, by contrast, may have greater flexibility to recover the cost through convenience fees, pricing or other monetisation mechanisms, according to Elara.

Food Delivery And Quick Commerce Largely Insulated

Despite high digital-payment penetration, food delivery and quick-commerce platforms are expected to see limited exposure because of their lower average order values. Elara estimates Zomato's food delivery average net order value at Rs 381 and Blinkit's at Rs 540. The resulting MDR costs are estimated at Rs 63 million and Rs 119 million, respectively.

At the consolidated Eternal level, the brokerage estimates an MDR impact of Rs 182 million, equivalent to 0.6 per cent of FY27 estimated Ebitda. For Swiggy, the estimated incremental MDR cost across its food delivery and Instamart businesses is Rs 86 million, translating into an estimated 0.4 per cent impact on consolidated Ebitda.

QSRs Face Minimal Impact

Quick-service restaurant (QSR) companies are expected to remain largely insulated because their average ticket sizes are significantly below the Rs 2,000 threshold. Elara estimates an average ticket size of around Rs 500 for the segment, with the potential Ebitda impact at around 0.1 per cent across the listed QSR companies covered in the report.

The brokerage estimates that Jubilant FoodWorks, Devyani International, Sapphire Foods, Restaurant Brands Asia and Westlife Foodworld would each face an Ebitda impact of around 0.1 per cent.

For Jubilant FoodWorks, the estimated MDR cost is Rs 11 million, while Devyani International, Sapphire Foods, Restaurant Brands Asia and Westlife Foodworld are estimated to face costs of Rs 6 million, Rs 4 million, Rs 4 million and Rs 4 million, respectively.

Trent Sees Limited Exposure

Trent is estimated to face an incremental MDR cost of around Rs 217 million, equivalent to 0.5 per cent of consolidated FY27 Ebitda. Elara estimates Westside's average order value at Rs 1,600 and Zudio's at Rs 900, with the lower ticket size at Zudio partly offsetting Westside's higher exposure.

The brokerage's estimates assume a 0.4 per cent MDR and that the cost is initially absorbed by merchants and platforms. If the cost is subsequently passed on to consumers, the actual Ebitda impact could be lower, Elara said.

Cost Recovery Could Limit Profitability Impact

Elara said companies could use several levers to offset the potential MDR burden, including higher advertising revenue, operational efficiencies, increased platform fees and modest increases in take rates. The brokerage therefore does not expect a material impact on its estimates for most consumer companies under coverage.

The report is based on Elara Securities' latest FY27 estimates and assumptions.

data.title: CBI Books Reliance Capital, Anil Ambani In Rs 2,684-Cr LIC Case
data.description:
LIC’s complaint alleges misrepresentation and diversion of funds invested in five NCDs issued by Reliance Capital between 2012 and 2018

Reliance Group chairman Anil Ambani has denied any wrongdoing after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a case against Reliance Capital (RCAP) over an alleged Rs 2,684.57-crore fraud involving investments made by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The FIR names RCAP, its former chairman, former group managing director Satish Seth, unidentified public servants and others.

The FIR was registered on the basis of a written complaint received from LIC, according to an official statement. The case relates to investments made by the insurer in RCAP and allegations including cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal misconduct, diversion or misappropriation of funds and falsification of accounts.

A spokesperson for Ambani said the FIR pertains to Reliance Capital and noted that Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director and Chairman of the company’s board from 2005 until November 2021. At that time, the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an Administrator.

Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law, the spokesperson added. The CBI’s case, meanwhile, concerns the allegations made in LIC’s complaint against RCAP, Ambani, Seth, unidentified public servants and others.

LIC Investments Under Probe

According to the CBI, LIC has alleged that it subscribed to five non-convertible debentures issued by RCAP between 12 April 2012, and 9 March 2018. The investments aggregated to Rs 3,900 crore and were made for general corporate purposes, funding requirements and refinancing of existing debt.

The CBI said LIC has alleged that the accused persons entered into a criminal conspiracy and committed offences including cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal misconduct, diversion or misappropriation of funds and falsification of accounts. These allegations form part of the complaint on which the FIR was registered.

LIC has alleged that the accused persons dishonestly induced it to invest in RCAP through misrepresentation and thereafter fraudulently diverted the funds. According to the CBI, the insurer has alleged that these actions resulted in a wrongful loss to LIC.

The CBI said LIC has alleged that the acts caused a wrongful loss of Rs 2,684.57 crore to the insurer. The complaint also alleges a corresponding wrongful gain to the accused persons and other beneficiaries, according to the agency.

CBI Traces Fund Movement

The CBI has taken up an investigation to identify the role of all those involved, including public servants and private individuals. The agency will also examine the alleged criminal conspiracy and trace the end-use or diversion of the invested funds.

The investigation covers the funds invested by LIC through the five NCDs issued by RCAP. The CBI said it would examine the allegations made in the complaint and trace the end-use or possible diversion of those investments.

The case remains under investigation, with the CBI examining the role of the individuals and entities named in the FIR. The agency’s probe will also cover the alleged criminal conspiracy and the movement of the funds invested by LIC.

The CBI said it had earlier registered eight FIRs against Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Capital Limited, Reliance Home Finance Limited, Reliance Commercial Finance Limited and Reliance Telecom Limited. The cases were based on complaints received from various public-sector banks, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and LIC.

The agency said it has so far filed six charge sheets and arrested seven accused persons in these cases. The CBI added that the cases remain under investigation and are being monitored by the Supreme Court.

data.title: Thermal Power Plants’ Coal Stocks Fall 42% YoY In August, Cover Drops To 9 Days
data.description:
Coal-based generation rose 13 per cent as transport constraints limited replenishment, leaving 51 plants with critically low stocks during August

Coal inventories at India’s thermal power plants fell around 42 per cent year-on-year to 29 million tonnes (MT) in August 2026 from 50 MT a year earlier, as higher electricity demand pushed up coal-based power generation and consumption, according to a Crisil Intelligence report.

Coal stock cover at power plants nearly halved to nine days from 17 days a year earlier, marking the lowest level since November 2023. The decline was concentrated among plants dependent on domestic coal, highlighting challenges in replenishing inventories as coal consumption increased during the period.

Between April and August, coal consumption by thermal power plants rose around 8 per cent year-on-year to 395 MT, while electricity demand increased 9.5 per cent. The rise in demand was driven by an unusually hot summer and a below-normal southwest monsoon, with cumulative rainfall between June and August 13 per cent below the long-period average.

Overall power generation increased around 10.5 per cent year-on-year during the five months, while renewable energy generation rose 20.7 per cent. Despite faster growth in renewable generation, coal-fired power continued to play a critical role in meeting round-the-clock electricity demand, keeping pressure on thermal plant inventories.

Critical Stocks Widen

In August, 51 of the country’s 190 thermal power plants were operating with critically low coal stocks, compared with 20 plants a year earlier. Most of these facilities depend on domestic coal, making the availability of transportation and timely replenishment important for maintaining adequate stock levels.

The Central Electricity Authority considers coal stocks at power plants critical when they fall 25 per cent below the normative level. Inventory pressure was particularly high in Rajasthan, where around 72 per cent of coal-based generation capacity was operating with critically low stocks, followed by Madhya Pradesh at 69 per cent and Andhra Pradesh at 60 per cent.

Bihar and Jharkhand also reported substantial pressure, with 45 per cent and 48 per cent of their coal-based capacity, respectively, operating with critically low stocks. The situation was less pronounced in Odisha and West Bengal, where only 10 per cent and 6 per cent of coal-based capacity, respectively, was in the critical category.

Crisil Intelligence Director Sehul Bhatt said pithead coal inventories moderated from a peak of 157 MT in early March 2026 to around 76 MT in August. The decline reflected the normalisation of elevated stocks accumulated earlier in the year, rather than a broad deterioration in coal availability.

Bhatt said current pithead inventories remained broadly aligned with the average of 76.1 MT recorded across August 2024 and 2025. He said the inventory position indicated that coal availability remained adequate despite the drawdown and that there was no material supply-side stress.

The report identified a mismatch between rising electricity demand and transportation capacity as the key challenge affecting coal inventories at thermal power plants. Prolonged rainfall across the eastern coal belt disrupted mining operations and hampered coal evacuation, restricting the pace at which supplies could reach generating stations.

Between April and August, rake loading increased around 5 per cent, while coal receipts at power plants rose only 3 per cent. This was slower than the 8 per cent increase in coal consumption, leaving incremental evacuation insufficient to replenish inventories at power plants at the required pace.

To ease the situation, Coal India permitted power plants with fuel supply agreements to lift additional coal by road alongside rail transportation from September 7, 2026. The additional road movement is expected to supplement rail-based evacuation and support supplies to plants facing lower inventory levels.

Dispatches Critical Ahead

Crisil Intelligence Associate Director Surbhi Kaushal expects electricity demand, coal-based generation, coal consumption and coal dispatches to power plants to grow in a narrow range of 6-7 per cent year-on-year during the second half of the fiscal year. Power demand is estimated at 860-870 billion units during the period.

Coal-based generation is expected to retain a 65-70 per cent share of India’s electricity mix, according to the report. Kaushal said adequate inventories at miners and improving evacuation logistics should allow higher dispatch requirements to be met comfortably, reducing the likelihood of prolonged inventory pressure.

The report views the recent decline in power plant coal stocks as a temporary logistical issue rather than a structural supply constraint. However, adverse weather could disrupt mining and evacuation further, while delays in improving rail availability and rake loading capacity could prolong pressure on plant-level inventories.

Crisil Intelligence said sustained higher coal dispatches would be essential to rebuild power plant stocks towards the historical average cover of 16-18 days. The pace of evacuation and replenishment will remain important as coal-based generation continues to meet a significant share of India’s electricity demand.

data.title: IDFC FIRST Bank Removes Forex Markup Across All Credit Cards
data.description:
The bank’s existing and new cardholders will automatically get zero forex markup on international transactions without any upgrade or spending requirement

IDFC FIRST Bank has removed foreign exchange markup charges across its entire credit card portfolio, allowing existing and new customers to make eligible international transactions without paying the additional forex fee.

The benefit is being extended automatically to all credit card customers, with no requirement to apply for a new card, upgrade an existing card or meet a minimum spending threshold. It covers international transactions such as overseas purchases, online payments, subscriptions and other eligible foreign-currency spends.

Zero Forex Markup Across Card Portfolio

Forex markup is an additional charge levied by card issuers when a transaction is made in a foreign currency. Depending on the card, the charge can range from 1 per cent to 3.5 per cent, with Goods and Services Tax applicable on the fee.

Under the new structure, the bank has removed this markup across its credit card portfolio. The move extends the zero-markup proposition beyond premium and travel-focused cards to a wider set of customers.

The bank has also clarified that the zero-markup benefit does not mean every cost associated with an international transaction is waived. Exchange rates, merchant charges, ATM fees and other transaction-specific costs may still apply.

Customers Can Continue Using Existing Cards

Customers do not need to switch to a new credit card to access the benefit. The change applies to both existing and new cardholders.

The bank has also said applicable Reward Points or cashback will continue under the respective card programmes, although the treatment of international transactions is subject to the terms applicable to individual cards.

Customers making payments overseas should also be mindful of dynamic currency conversion. Choosing to pay in the local currency generally allows the transaction to be processed under the card's foreign-currency conversion terms, while choosing Indian rupees at an overseas merchant or ATM can involve a separate conversion charge.

The move comes as Indian banks and fintech companies increasingly compete on international spending benefits, particularly as overseas travel and cross-border online purchases gain traction.

data.title: Oil prices are high but could be much worse, Trump has China's Xi to thank for that
data.description:
It could be much worse.

When President Donald Trump launched his war against Iran in late February, energy analysts issued dire warnings that oil prices could more than double during a protracted conflict and urged investors and motorists to buckle up for a bumpy ride.

The war grinds on, and oil prices certainly remain volatile. But the most dire projections have not yet come to pass six months into a conflict that has no end in sight.

Chinese President Xi Jinping, who is making a much-anticipated state visit to Washington next week, could make a credible argument that the world has his country’s energy strategy to thank for that.

It’s unclear how much the two leaders will discuss Iran during the visit, which comes as Trump’s Republican Party faces pressure from voters over high gasoline prices, and as China’s buffer is being further tested as the conflict in the Middle East spreads. Trump, who has sought to keep a fragile trade truce with Beijing intact, has been careful in public comments about differences with Xi over the country’s relationship with Iran.

“We’ve been free-riding off Beijing in a weird way,” said Rosemary Kelanic, director of the Middle East program at Defence Priorities, a Washington think tank. “China’s doing it because they understand that they’re on the train that Trump is driving off a cliff. If oil prices go way up, that hurts the global economy. If it hurts the global economy, it hurts them.”

China’s stockpiles helped Xi weather the storm so far

Beijing spent years and billions of dollars amassing the world’s largest oil stockpile, building its strategic reserve to about 1.4 billion barrels by the end of last year, according to the US Energy Information Administration’s estimates. To protect China from foreign supply risks, Xi made energy self-reliance a part of the country’s latest five-year plan.

Drawing from the massive stockpile allowed China, the world’s second-biggest oil consumer and Iran’s top buyer, to dramatically cut crude imports once the US and Israel began their bombardment and Tehran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. The country was also helped by its shift toward electric vehicles in recent years and increasingly tapping into other energy alternatives.

China’s oil import diet in turn helped ease global demand, softening the upward price effects for the United States, Europe and beyond.

“The Chinese deserve credit,” said retired US Navy Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery, an analyst at the Foundation for Defence of Democracies, a hawkish Washington think tank. “They did in 10 years what took us 25 years after the 1973 oil crisis to do: really build a kind of strategic petroleum reserve that could allow you to weather this.” But that resilience faces new challenges. Attacks by Iran-backed militias this month led Saudi Arabia to temporarily shut a vital pipeline that transports crude across the kingdom to ports on the Red Sea.

The Yemen-based Houthis have also seized two strategic islands in the southern Red Sea, bolstering the Iran-backed rebels’ ability to disrupt a key maritime shipping route. Planned talks among Gulf nations focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which were supposed to take place earlier this week, have also been put on hold.

Before he meets Xi, Trump is set to meet Tuesday with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council in New York, on the sidelines of the annual United Nations General Assembly. The group includes Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain.

Oil industry experts say the moment remains tenuous

Analysts at Bank of America last week forecast oil at $83 a barrel for the second half of the year “in light of more persistent disruptions to Hormuz,” but said they still expected shipping through the strait to gradually pick up.

But if violence escalates and keeps a chokehold on traffic, prices could reach $95 to $120 a barrel, while damage to major energy infrastructure could produce spikes of up to $150 a barrel, the analysts wrote.

Brent crude averaged about $69 per barrel last year and currently is hovering around $100. Brent crude briefly peaked in late April, touching $126.

How China has weathered the volatile oil market caused by Trump’s war is ultimately seen by Beijing as “a vindication of Xi’s last five-year plan and his focus on self-reliance,” said Jonathan Czin, a former senior CIA analyst who is now at the Brookings Institution.

Deep differences between Trump and Xi on Iran persist

The war in Iran — and its impact on the global economy — is expected to be on the agenda for the Trump-Xi talks. But the prospects of the world’s two biggest powers coming up with a breakthrough appear dim.

Over the course of the conflict, the Trump administration has faced resistance when urging Beijing to use its considerable economic leverage to press the Islamic Republic to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Chinese officials, who have expressed strong opposition to the US war, also have bristled at more recent administration threats to ratchet up economic pressure on nations and entities still doing business with Iran.

To be certain, analysts say there’s little altruism in how China came to sit on its massive stockpile of oil.

Experts believe Beijing was driven by contingency planning for potential military action to take over the self-ruled island of Taiwan, which China considers its own territory. Tapping the reserves now has been far from ideal for Beijing — but seeing global oil prices skyrocket was not ideal, either.

Trump treads carefully on differences with China over Iran

The leaders last met in Beijing just four months ago, and could meet twice more later this year.

After the talks in May, Trump claimed Xi agreed with him that a nuclear-armed Iran is a bad idea and that the Strait of Hormuz must be reopened. Chinese officials have neither affirmed nor denied Trump’s telling of the private conversation.

The US administration has also warned China not to aid Iran’s military effort. But earlier this week, Trump downplayed a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities had supplied Tehran with satellite images of a Jordanian military base ahead of an Iran strike in July that killed three US soldiers working there.

“You know, when they say that China spies on us, I say you’re right, and we spy on them too,” Trump told reporters.

Trump at the outset of the war called the conflict a “little excursion” that would last a matter of weeks.

He also has repeatedly predicted that oil prices will quickly plummet once the conflict ends. Less than three months into the conflict, he even declared “everybody was wrong” because the most dire projections for oil prices didn’t come to pass.

The White House did not respond to queries on whether Trump credits China’s actions with helping keep oil prices from hitting the worst-case levels.

But energy analysts credit Beijing’s slashing imports as having the single greatest impact on moderating prices since the start of the war. China’s crude imports averaged just 8.1 million barrels per day in the second quarter. That’s almost 4 million barrels per day, or 32% lower than in the first three months of the year, according to US data.

“It’s remarkable how China managed the market,” said Michael Lynch, president of Strategic Energy and Economic Research, a firm providing consulting services and analysis in the oil and gas industry. “They didn’t panic and by turning to their inventories they kept the price down for everybody.”
